summary: iter22 — MarksEntryModal multi-subject grid (size=xl). Live-verified end-to-end as school_admin (principal@sunrise.edu) on /school/exams against the seeded Mid-Term (Grade 5) exam. Behaviors confirmed: (a) modal opens with no marks-subject dropdown, (b) renders exactly 5 columns marks-col-<sid> for Mathematics/Science/English/Social Studies/Hindi, (c) each header carries an editable Out-of input (marks-max-<sid>) defaulting to existing exam max or 100, (d) each student row has marks-input-<UID>-<sid> per subject (8 students × 5 subjects = 40 cells), (e) existing saved marks pre-populate both Out-of and per-student cells, (f) Save button labeled 'Save all marks', (g) successful save toast 'Saved N marks across 5 subjects' and modal auto-closes, (h) client-side validation toast 'Vihaan Patel · Science: marks must be between 0 and 50' captured when an existing mark exceeds a newly-lowered Out-of — modal correctly stays open so the user can fix, (i) blank/0 Out-of yields 'Set a valid \'Out of\' for <subject>' (validation logic path read in code; toast read intermittent due to brief react-hot-toast lifetime). Subject IDs detected end-to-end via marks-col-<id> data-testids and confirmed unique per subject. No console errors during the multi-subject flow other than the expected pre-login 401 probe.

issues: When user lowers Out-of below an already-saved mark for another student, save is correctly blocked but the error message only names one offender at a time — multi-error summary would speed bulk corrections. Acceptable for v1.

critical_code_review_comments: ExamsPage.jsx:117-140 useEffect dependency list (exam.id, exam.class_id, exam.section) is correct; cancelled flag prevents state updates on stale promises. Good.

ExamsPage.jsx:154-194 save() validates BEFORE any network call so partial writes are avoided across subjects. Each subject is a separate POST /marks/bulk; if a later subject errors mid-loop, earlier subjects already persisted — consider wrapping with a 'savedSubjects' list to roll-forward-warn rather than just toast formatApiError. Currently low risk because client-side validation runs upfront.

ExamsPage.jsx:173-189 The save loop re-sends EVERY pre-loaded student entry per subject on every save, even for students the user did not touch. This is functionally correct (idempotent upsert) but inflates network usage by ~Nstudents×Nsubjects on each save. For 8×5 it's 40 docs/save which is fine; at 50×10 (500/save) it may become noticeable. Optional: diff against initial snapshot.

ExamsPage.jsx:149-152 setMax clamps min to 1 (Math.max(1, Number(value))) but allows blank ('') in state to support validation toast — good UX. Same path correctly rejects on save via 'if (!mx || mx <= 0)'.

ExamsPage.jsx:212-235 Sticky left columns (Roll 60px, UID 90px @ left-[60px], Student 160px @ left-[150px]) — left-offset 150 is correct (60+90). Background bg-bg-surface keeps stickies opaque over scroll. Good.
ExamsPage.jsx:250 Over-range cell border 'border-status-danger text-status-danger' gives immediate visual feedback before save — nice UX.

ExamsPage.jsx:113 subjectMax default initializer Object.fromEntries((subjects||[]).map(s=>[s.id,100])) is recomputed on every render via useState lazy initializer which is fine, but subsequent prop changes to subjects (rare here) would not refresh defaults; acceptable because subjects are loaded once in parent.

UX consideration (not a bug): When user reduces Out-of below already-saved seed marks for OTHER students, validation correctly blocks save but message only flags first offender. Confirm with product whether bulk-flagging all offending cells (highlight + count) is desirable. Currently the visual red-border on cells already does this — just no aggregated toast.

success_rate.frontend: 100% — multi-subject grid render, per-subject Out-of edit, multi-cell entry, save loop, client-side validation, persistence on reopen all verified

context_for_next_testing_agent: MarksEntryModal selectors: marks-entry-modal (Modal wrapper), marks-grid-wrap (scroll container), marks-col-<subject_id> (per-subject column header), marks-max-<subject_id> (Out-of input), marks-input-<student_uid>-<subject_id> (mark cell, note: UID like STU-00001), marks-row-<student_uid>, save-marks-btn. The dropdown 'marks-subject' is removed and must NOT be re-added. Backend POST /api/marks/bulk is called once per subject with non-empty entries; max_marks is sent per request so each saved mark doc carries its own subject-specific max — confirmed via persistence reload (max read back from response). When testing 'lower Out-of than seed mark' scenarios on the DEMO Mid-Term exam, pre-existing seed marks (e.g., Mathematics: Aarav=87, Diya=91; Science: Vihaan=64) will trigger validation — the test plan's 'set max=80 and Aarav=70 → save success' is only achievable on a fresh exam OR by also editing the conflicting students' marks down to <=80 in the same save. The current code handles this correctly by rejecting with a precise toast that names the student and subject; modal stays open so user can fix in place.
rca of the issue: No bug found. Apparent 'persistence failure' during one test pass was actually correct rejection by client-side validation when the proposed Out-of (80) was below pre-seeded marks (Aarav=87, Diya=91 in Mathematics). Validation message captured during Science test confirmed the same code path: 'Vihaan Patel · Science: marks must be between 0 and 50'. Toast component (react-hot-toast) has a short lifetime and unmounts before some polling read_toast() calls fired; using a slightly longer settle (≥2s after click on save-marks-btn before scraping toast text) gives consistent capture. Recommend the main agent and future testing agents use a clean-exam fixture or explicitly clear conflicting cells before lowering Out-of when scripting positive-path saves.
